correctness.rationale: Exact Euclidean least-norm weights w_i=1/n-m(X_i-m)/S follow from two affine constraints. Polar coordinates Xi=m+r a_i on H_n have Jacobian sqrt(n) r^{n-2} and uniform bounds |m|A(a)/r-1 <= kappa <= |m|A(a)/r+1. Integrating the collision near r=0 by dominated convergence for bounded compactly supported a.e.-continuous densities, or using Gaussian factorization, gives exact t^{-(n-1)} asymptotic coefficient with the angular integral and finite positive constant. Tail integration proves E[kappa^p]<infinity iff p<n-1; noise variance iff n>3. Independent Gaussian moment/angular integration and Monte Carlo corroborate C2=2/pi, C3=2/9+sqrt3/(3pi). In n=3 independent Gaussian mean and residual polar variables give all weights positive probability (3/(pi sqrt3)) F(pi/3|2/3)=.654208764956, below feasibility 3/4. This exact conditional geometry, not simulation, proves the claimed law.
